title: Understanding Blood Pressure
simple_explanation: Blood pressure is the measure of the force that your heart uses to pump blood around your body through your blood vessels. It is recorded using two numbers: Systolic (the top number, representing pressure during a heartbeat) and Diastolic (the bottom number, representing pressure when the heart rests between beats).
important_points: Blood pressure varies naturally throughout the day based on activity, stress, and caffeine intake.
A single high reading does not automatically mean you have hypertension.
Proper cuff size and resting quietly for 5 minutes before measurement ensures accurate readings.

common_medical_terms.definition: Pressure in arteries when the heart contracts.
Pressure in arteries when the heart rests between beats.
Persistently elevated blood pressure above typical baseline ranges.

general_health_awareness: Regular physical activity, reducing sodium intake, managing stress, and maintaining a balanced diet help support healthy blood pressure levels.
when_to_consult: Consult a doctor if your blood pressure is consistently elevated, or immediately if severe high readings are accompanied by chest pain, severe headache, or shortness of breath.
disclaimer: This information is educational only. Blood pressure ranges must be evaluated by a healthcare professional in light of your individual health history.

title: Complete Blood Count (CBC) Basics
simple_explanation: A Complete Blood Count (CBC) is a common blood test that measures different components of your blood, including red blood cells, white blood cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelets. It provides a general snapshot of your overall health.
important_points: Hemoglobin carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body.
White Blood Cells (WBCs) are part of the immune system that helps defend against infection.
Platelets help the blood clot to prevent excessive bleeding when injured.

common_medical_terms.definition: An iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
The number of infection-fighting white blood cells in a sample.
Cell fragments that play a critical role in blood clotting.

general_health_awareness: CBC tests are widely used during routine checkups or to investigate symptoms like fatigue, fever, or unexplained bruising.
when_to_consult: Always discuss lab test values with your prescribing physician. Reference ranges vary by laboratory, age, sex, and health history.
disclaimer: Laboratory parameters require professional clinical context. Never attempt self-diagnosis based solely on raw laboratory numbers.

title: Understanding Fasting Blood Glucose
simple_explanation: A fasting blood glucose test measures the concentration of glucose (sugar) in your blood after an overnight fast of at least 8 hours. It is used to assess how effectively your body processes sugar.
important_points: Fasting for 8 to 12 hours (water is permitted) is required for accurate results.
Glucose is the primary source of energy for your body's cells, derived from food.
Hormones like insulin help regulate glucose levels in the bloodstream.

common_medical_terms.definition: A simple sugar that serves as the body's main energy source.
A hormone produced by the pancreas that allows sugar to enter cells.
Elevated level of glucose in the blood.

general_health_awareness: Maintaining a balanced diet rich in whole foods, exercising regularly, and avoiding excessive refined sugars help maintain healthy blood sugar regulation.
when_to_consult: Consult a doctor if you experience persistent symptoms such as increased thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss, or fatigue.
disclaimer: This note provides general educational information and is not a diagnostic tool for diabetes or metabolic disorders.
